Laura / Ben — see proposed approach below. High-level: we can accept defend-and-control in customer-facing Order Forms for third-party IP claims tied to model output, but only if we get the following operational and contractual protections. Proposed draft language and operational guardrails are attached.

Key legal guardrails (summary):
- Narrow trigger: claim must allege infringement arising from customer-provided content or outputs directly generated by the contracted model configuration. Not a broad training-data / model ownership claim.
- Notice cadence: initial notice (email) with summary within 7 days; Redwood has 30 days (from notice) to accept defense or propose remediation plan.
- Evidence & custody: customer must provide the evidence template items (timestamps, prompts, outputs, account IDs). Evidence upload via secure S3 presigned link or secure portal. Redwood will designate an "Evidence Custodian" (we) for technical artifacts; counsel involvement kept privileged.
- Privilege / confidentiality: preserve Redwood privilege for internal investigation materials; redaction process for customer PII.
- Insurance / cap: we propose a per-claim cap equal to the greater of (3x annual fee) or $1M, subject to insurance offset and subrogation carveouts.
- Canary / fallback: if the claim is clearly outside the narrow trigger (e.g., challenge to model training dataset licensing), Redwood reserves the right to reimburse up to the cap instead of defend.

Operational additions:
- Evidence template (we should accept their template but add a required minimum set).
- A two-person on-call rotation (Eng + Legal) for initial triage during business hours.
- A runbook link to be included in onboarding materials.

Attachments: proposed_redline_excerpt.txt (snippet of MSA paragraph), operational_runbook_v1.pdf (stub).

If Ben can confirm commercial flexibility, I'll prepare an Order Form redline that maps the cap/insurance offset and inserts the evidence upload link and triage SLA.

Kim

Tom — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. I'm copying Laura and Kimberly who have proposed guardrails. Two commercial notes from our side:

1) Cap & insurance offset: Redwood can accept defend-and-control if we align on a per-claim cap (proposed: greater of $1M or 3x annual fees) with standard insurance offset language (we subtract recoveries from insurance proceeds).

2) Commercial trade: To close this quickly, Redwood is prepared to offer a 12-month credit equivalent to 5% of committed spend if Acme signs a 12-month dedicated order form and accepts the proposed evidence/cadence mechanics.

Operational ask: please confirm the procurement timeline and where you'll upload evidence artifacts (we prefer a secure S3 presigned link; if you require an on-prem portal, let's flag that now). I'll also drop the updated Order Form (with cap and evidence link) in DocuSign once legal and procurement align.
